evals.name: projection-level-key
evals.prompt:
This Screenplay projection leaves `status` empty after InvoiceSent. InvoiceSent carries `invoiceId`, which differs from its event source id. Explain and fix it. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.

```
projection InvoiceDetails => InvoiceDetailsReadModel
  key invoiceId
  from InvoiceRegistered key invoiceId
    status = "draft"
  from InvoiceSent
    status = "sent"
```
evals.expected_output: A projection-level `key` routes nothing (warning PLAY0381). A `from` without a key does not inherit another `from`'s key; it defaults to the event source id, so InvoiceSent updates a different instance. Remove the projection-level key and write `from InvoiceSent key invoiceId`.
assertions: Says the projection-level `key` parses but routes no event and produces warning PLAY0381.
Says a `from` without a key does not inherit another `from`'s key and defaults to the event source id.
Fixes it by keying each `from` (`from InvoiceSent key invoiceId`) and removing the projection-level key.
Advises running the compiler with warnings as errors.

evals.name: every-versus-all
evals.prompt: In a Screenplay projection for an Invoice I want lastUpdatedAt to change on invoice events but not when a line-item child event arrives, and separately a counter of every event type per event source. Which blocks do I use and what are the pitfalls? Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Use `every` with `exclude children` for lastUpdatedAt: `every` fires only for event types named in the level's `from` and `join` blocks. Use `all` for the per-source counters over every event type in the system. They are not synonyms. `all` inside `children` or `nested` behaves as `every` (PLAY0380), and `exclude children` is not accepted inside a children block.
assertions: Uses `every` with `exclude children` for the lastUpdatedAt mapping.
States that `every` fires only for the event types its level names in `from` and `join` blocks.
Uses `all` for the system-wide counters and says `all` fires for every event type in the system.
Warns that confusing `all` and `every` is the classic mistake, and that `all` inside `children` or `nested` behaves as `every` (PLAY0380).

evals.name: join-never-creates
evals.prompt: InvoiceDetails should show the customer name. CustomerRenamed carries customerId and name. A colleague wrote `join customer on customerId` with `with CustomerRenamed` and expects an InvoiceDetails row to appear for a customer with no invoice yet. Explain what happens and what shapes the instance. Reply only; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A join never creates an instance (PLAY0063, PLAY0064). `join <label> on <property>` followed by `with <EventType>` only maps onto an instance that a `from` block created, so no row appears. An unmatched `with` event does nothing.
assertions: States that a join never creates an instance.
Describes the shape `join <label> on <property>` followed by `with <EventType>` blocks.
Says instances come from `from` blocks, so a customer without an invoice produces no InvoiceDetails row.
Mentions that automap or `no automap` under a joined event follows the level the join sits in.

evals.name: reducer-vs-projection
evals.prompt: An Order read model needs a lifecycle state machine whose next state depends on the current state, so a teammate wants a reducer. Show the reducer shape in Screenplay and say what the reference runner and specifications can do with it. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: Use `reducer OrderLifecycle => OrderState` with an `on` rule per event, each with a body (tagged fence or `file`). `context.State` is null for the first event, the key is always the event source id, and returning null deletes the instance. The body is opaque, so a specification reading a reducer-built read model reports unsupported and never passes in the reference runner. Prefer a projection where one will do.
assertions: Writes `reducer <Name> => <ReadModel>` with `on <Event>` rules that each have a body in a tagged fence or a `file`.
Says `context.State` is null for the first event and that the key is always the event source id.
Says the reference runner cannot compute reducer state, so a specification reading it reports unsupported and never passes.
Says a reducer is code and a projection is preferred wherever one will do.
